# Paired public Library browser fixture

The optional fixture-owned `mir5-library-paired-browser-retained-refresh` Boolean defaults false. An explicit arm projection may package `settings-updates-retained.lua` as `settings-updates.lua` to enable600 baseline ticks,32 alternating public refreshes at30-tick intervals and600 post-refresh ticks after the existing cold-reopen/render checks. Four peer markers preserve exact ticks,iteration counts and unchanged native state;the existing twelve screenshots and four profiled actions remain. This observes refresh churn,with actual keyboard close/open and player removal remaining separate.

The proposed [measurement method](../../../spec/evidence/library-peak-retained-method-r01.json) distinctly names OS lifetime peaks,periodic diagnostics and retained-window medians under existing tolerances. Independent review,native preflight and a final exact-input freeze are required before scoring. Host controls and this file establish no native performance or release verdict;earlier failed controls remain unchanged.

This F200 fixture is a future performance-input witness, not a timing result. It
uses only the historical public `more-infinite-research-browser.open` interface
and native GUI objects; it never imports MIR Lua modules, reads MIR storage,
raises GUI events, completes research, or changes package tuning.

The selected profile enables exactly one arm selector. The selector changes only
the fixture-owned startup setting `mir5-library-paired-browser-arm` before the
ordinary `Defaults` setting mode is read:

| Arm | MIR package | selector | public GUI record |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `published` | 4.7.20002 | `arm-published` | `mir_browser_*` search/results/detail names |
| `mir5` | 5.0.20000 | `arm-mir5` | `mir_library_*` query/results/detail names |

The published arm is pinned to archive `F3943EB4…1010B7`. The candidate arm is pinned to the F200 package from source `8bfb0d99`, archive `2BBDBA9A…F9E842`. These are selected inputs, not matched performance results.

A post-load server emits its one `ready` marker on its first runtime event; the
create-only seed's `on_init` marker is not reused as readiness for the ordinary
host. Each real client join is recorded as the bounded ordered sequence
`MIR5English 1`, `MIR5Deutsch 2`, then after the cold restart `MIR5English 3`,
`MIR5Deutsch 4`. After the first two clients join one fresh Base F200 force,
each of `first-open`, `search`, and `refresh` wraps exactly two public open
calls in one native profiler record, then requests one screenshot per client.
The fixture saves a restart point, requires an actual cold host restart and
rejoin, then performs `reopen` the same way. The original eight immediate PNGs and four raw profiler markers remain. The current diagnostic fixture additionally captures both unchanged first-open roots after 60 ticks, before search, and both unchanged reopened roots after 60 ticks, before completion. These four extra captures occur outside the profiler, without another public open call; native state, query and selected detail are checked again. A replaced or invalid root fails explicitly. Exactly twelve PNGs are now required under `script-output/mir5-library-paired-browser/`, with `first-open-settled` and `reopen-settled` added to the original labels. The shared profiler reader's first action token remains `first_open`. Earlier eight-image datasets retain their original fixture and verdict; the new protocol is a changed diagnostic input requiring its own freeze.

The R01 native performance dataset exposed a missing cold-load readiness witness: the original fixture queued `ready` only for its initial saved world. The current fixture queues exactly one `ready` marker on the first runtime event after either actual load, using local flags only during `on_load`; it still waits for the two new clients and the original settlement delay before reopening. This observation correction qualifies no old missing measurement, changes no player code, and requires its own declared input hash before a replacement native experiment.

The later matched-view fixture explicitly submits `family="all"` to both public interfaces. Their defaults differ: the original R01 screenshots show published All research and candidate MIR research. After each action and at both delayed captures, the fixture checks the actual native family dropdown's selected `mir-browser.scope-all` value. The published unnamed dropdown is found only within its bounded existing filter flows; missing, duplicate, wrong or changed scope refuses. Action markers carry the requested family and a strict native-verification flag that the session reader requires. This changes future fixture/method inputs only. Frozen R01/R02 diagnostic runs keep their original source, default-view discrepancy, stopping rules and unaccepted status; no replacement acceptance dataset is declared by this correction. Native preflight and independent protocol review must precede any new scored dataset.

At every action boundary it compares a bounded public snapshot of two named
technologies, two recipes, the current research/progress, and an at-most-eight
entry queue. The ordinary fresh seed must have no active or queued research.
These checks show the public browser did not mutate the named native state;
they do not establish live Library refresh, product tuning, screenshot rendering,
process memory, timing acceptance, or a release result. The existing
`library-multiplayer` fixture remains the separate current-candidate functional
scenario with its lab, queue, foreign-force, and ten-capture obligations.

The delayed first-open screenshot request is followed by a separate60-tick render grace before search changes the GUI. Native R02 showed that changing the GUI in the screenshot-request tick renders the following query in that image;the original images and adverse interpretation remain retained. This preparation needs native confirmation of the captured query before a replacement dataset.

Future paired create-only seeds use the explicit `--map-gen-seed 424242` argument, restricted to this case in the shared native runner. Each creation/initial-host/cold-host `ready` marker reads the actual first surface and refuses a missing surface, missing map settings or different seed; it records the complete native `map_gen_settings` for independent parsed comparison between arms and loads. Other fixture creation arguments remain unchanged. The [documented CLI seed parameter](https://wiki.factorio.com/Command_line_parameters) is an input control, not proof that the earlier defaults produced different terrain or caused failed memory controls. Native preflight must verify equal actual map settings and captured workloads before a separate reviewed replacement schedule; all original receipts retain their own inputs and failures.

The later counter/render preflight observed the final-save modal over the current late cold-reopen captures: the save was requested in the screenshot-request tick. Future fixtures retain a separate60-tick grace after `reopen-settled` before the completion marker/final save, checking both original roots, queries and All scope again before saving. It adds no screenshot or public call and stays outside all four profiled actions. The original modal-obscured frames and counter-availability result remain retained; corrected native image preflight must accompany fixed-map verification before scoring.
